### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Customer reviews for products with ratings (1-5 stars) and optional text
content

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Referenced customer's shopping_mall_customers.id
- `order_item_id`: Referenced order item's shopping_mall_order_items.id
- `rating`: Rating score from 1 to 5 stars given by customer
- `content`: Optional text content of the review written by customer

### `shopping_mall_review_snapshots`

Review snapshots preserving state at time of edit or deletion. This table
stores complete copies of customer reviews when they are modified,
creating an immutable audit trail of all review changes. Each snapshot
captures the review content, rating, and user information as it existed
at the time of the edit or deletion, enabling historical analysis and
dispute resolution.

Key relationships: References the original review in
shopping_mall_reviews table, allowing retrieval of the current review
state alongside its historical snapshots. Multiple snapshots can exist
for a single review, creating a complete history of all modifications.

**IMPORTANT**: This is an immutable audit table - snapshots should never
be modified or deleted once created, preserving the historical record for
compliance and dispute resolution purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for each review snapshot record.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`
  > Original review's [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews) that this snapshot
  > captures.
- `customer_id`: Customer who wrote the review's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `product_id`: Product that was reviewed's [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `rating`
  > Star rating given by the customer (1-5 stars). Captured rating value at
  > time of snapshot.
- `text`
  > Text content of the review. Will be '[review deleted]' if review was
  > deleted.
- `edited_at`
  > When the original review was edited (if applicable). Null if this is the
  > original snapshot.
- `created_at`: When this snapshot was created (timestamp of the edit/delete action).

### `shopping_mall_product_review_ratings`

Aggregated product ratings calculated from customer reviews.

This table stores computed rating metrics for each product in the
shopping mall platform. It maintains real-time aggregation of customer
review data including average rating scores and review counts.

## Business Purpose

- **Rating Aggregation**: Calculates and stores average ratings from
customer reviews
- **Review Counting**: Maintains accurate count of non-deleted reviews
per product
- **Performance Optimization**: Provides fast access to rating
information without real-time aggregation
- **Product Display**: Enables display of rating metrics in product
listings and search results

## Key Relationships

- References: [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products) - The product being rated
- References: [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews) - Individual customer
reviews (via foreign key)

## Important Notes

- Ratings are automatically updated when reviews are added, edited, or
deleted
- Deleted reviews are excluded from rating calculations
- The average_rating field stores decimal values (e.g., 4.5 stars)
- This table enables efficient product sorting and filtering by rating

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: Product being rated. References [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `average_rating`: Average rating calculated from customer reviews (1.0-5.0 scale).
- `review_count`: Total count of non-deleted customer reviews.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Record deletion timestamp (soft delete). Nullable for active records.

state at time of edit. Each snapshot captures the cancellation request
details including customer request reason, seller response reason (if
any), current status, and timestamps. Used for audit trail and dispute
resolution when cancellation requests are updated.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id`
  > The cancellation request that this snapshot represents. {@link
  > shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.

  > The customer who created the original cancellation request. {@link

- `seller_id`

  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `seller_session_id`
  > Seller session context when the response was made (if any). {@link
  > shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id}.
- `request_reason`
  > The customer's reason for requesting cancellation at the time of
  > snapshot. Copy of cancellation request reason field.
- `response_reason`
  > The seller's response reason at the time of snapshot. Null if no response
  > was given yet.
- `status`
  > The cancellation request status at the time of snapshot. Values:
  > 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created (when the original cancellation
  > request was created or last updated).

- `order_item_title`: Order item being refunded
- `requested_amount`: Refund amount requested by customer

- `customer_preferred_refund`

- `processing_fee`: Refund processing fee charged to customer

- `request_timestamp`: Timestamp of the refund request creation
- `response_timestamp`: Timestamp when seller responded to the refund request
- `created_by`: User who created this snapshot (customer or seller)
- `state_snapshot`: Complete refund state as JSON snapshot for detailed audit

instruction:
Create the complete API interface specification for an e-commerce shopping mall platform based on the following requirements:

## API Design Philosophy
- RESTful design principles with clear resource hierarchy
- JWT-based authentication with Bearer tokens
- Comprehensive OpenAPI 3.0 documentation
- TypeScript DTOs with full type safety
- Standardized response format with consistent error handling

## Core API Modules

### 1. Authentication & User Management
**Authentication Endpoints**
- `POST /auth/register-customer` - Register new customer
- `POST /auth/register-seller` - Register new seller
- `POST /auth/login` - User login with email/password
- `POST /auth/refresh` - Refresh authentication token
- `POST /auth/logout` - User logout
- `POST /auth/password/change` - Change password
- `GET /auth/me` - Get current user profile

**User Management**
- `DELETE /users/me` - Delete own account
- `GET /users/:id` - Get user profile
- `PATCH /users/:id` - Update user profile information

### 2. Customer Profile & Addresses
**Customer Profile**
- `GET /customers/me` - Get current customer profile
- `PATCH /customers/me` - Update customer profile (name, phone)

**Shipping Addresses**
- `GET /customers/me/addresses` - List all customer addresses
- `POST /customers/me/addresses` - Create new address
- `GET /customers/me/addresses/:id` - Get specific address
- `PATCH /customers/me/addresses/:id` - Update address
- `DELETE /customers/me/addresses/:id` - Delete address
- `PATCH /customers/me/addresses/:id/set-default` - Set as default address

### 3. Seller Management
**Seller Account Operations**
- `GET /sellers/me` - Get current seller profile
- `PATCH /sellers/me` - Update seller profile (shop name, description, logo)
- `DELETE /sellers/me` - Delete seller account (with validation)

**Seller Profile Management**
- `GET /sellers/:id` - Get seller profile by ID
- `GET /sellers/:id/history` - Get seller profile change history (snapshots)
- `POST /sellers/:id/approval/reapply` - Reapply for seller approval after rejection

**Seller Dashboard**
- `GET /sellers/me/dashboard` - Get seller dashboard summary statistics
- `GET /sellers/me/orders` - List seller's order items (paginated, filtered by status)

### 4. Administrator Management
**Admin System**
- `POST /admins/request` - Request to become administrator
- `GET /admins/me` - Get current admin profile and permissions

**Super Administrator Only**
- `GET /admins/pending-requests` - List pending admin requests
- `PATCH /admins/pending-requests/:id/approve` - Approve admin request
- `PATCH /admins/pending-requests/:id/reject` - Reject admin request
- `PATCH /admins/:id/promote-to-super` - Promote admin to super admin
- `PATCH /admins/:id/demote-to-regular` - Demote super admin to regular
- `GET /admins/super-admins` - List all super administrators

### 5. Category Management
**Public Categories**
- `GET /categories` - List all categories (paginated)
- `GET /categories/:id` - Get category details with subcategories
- `GET /categories/:id/products` - Get products in category (paginated, with filters)

**Admin Category Management**
- `POST /admin/categories` - Create category (admin only)
- `PATCH /admin/categories/:id` - Update category (admin only)
- `DELETE /admin/categories/:id` - Delete category (admin only) - products become uncategorized

### 6. Product Management
**Public Product Access**
- `GET /products` - List all products (paginated, searchable, filterable)
- `GET /products/:id` - Get product details with all variants
- `GET /products/:id/snapshots` - Get product change history (public view)

**Seller Product Management**
- `POST /sellers/me/products` - Create new product
- `PATCH /sellers/me/products/:id` - Update product
- `DELETE /sellers/me/products/:id` - Delete product (with validation)
- `GET /sellers/me/products` - List seller's products (paginated, filtered)
- `GET /sellers/me/products/:id/snapshots` - Get seller's product history

**Product Images**
- `POST /sellers/me/products/:id/images` - Upload product images
- `PATCH /sellers/me/products/:id/images/order` - Reorder images
- `DELETE /sellers/me/products/:id/images/:imageId` - Delete specific image

**Admin Product Oversight**
- `GET /admin/products` - List all platform products (paginated, filtered)
- `DELETE /admin/products/:id` - Admin delete product (policy violations)
- `GET /admin/products/:id/snapshots` - Admin view any product history

**Product Search & Filtering**
- `GET /products/search` - Search products by name
- Filter parameters: category, minPrice, maxPrice, inStockOnly
- Sort parameters: newest, price-asc, price-desc

### 7. Product Variants & Inventory
**Product Variants**
- `POST /sellers/me/products/:id/variants` - Add variants to product
- `PATCH /sellers/me/products/:productId/variants/:variantId` - Update variant
- `DELETE /sellers/me/products/:productId/variants/:variantId` - Delete variant (with validation)
- `GET /products/:id/variants` - Get all variants for product

**Inventory Management**
- `POST /sellers/me/inventory` - Add/subtract inventory (restock/adjustment)
- `GET /sellers/me/inventory/:variantId` - Get inventory history for variant
- `GET /products/:id/variants/:variantId/stock` - Check variant stock level

### 8. Product Snapshots
**Snapshot Access**
- `GET /products/:id/snapshots` - Get product snapshots (customer/seller view)
- `GET /products/:id/snapshots/:snapshotId` - Get specific snapshot details
- `GET /sellers/me/products/:id/snapshots` - Seller's product snapshots
- `GET /admin/products/:id/snapshots` - Admin product snapshots

### 9. Wishlist Management
- `GET /customers/me/wishlist` - List customer wishlist (paginated)
- `POST /customers/me/wishlist` - Add product to wishlist
- `DELETE /customers/me/wishlist/:productId` - Remove product from wishlist
- `GET /customers/me/wishlist/availability` - Check wishlist availability status

### 10. Shopping Cart
- `GET /customers/me/cart` - Get customer cart
- `POST /customers/me/cart` - Add variant to cart
- `PATCH /customers/me/cart/items/:itemId` - Update cart item quantity
- `DELETE /customers/me/cart/items/:itemId` - Remove item from cart
- `POST /customers/me/cart/validate` - Validate cart (stock checks, availability)

### 11. Order Management
**Order Placement**
- `POST /orders` - Create order from cart (checkout)
- `GET /orders/:id` - Get order details
- `GET /customers/me/orders` - List customer orders (paginated, sorted by newest first)

**Order Status Tracking**
- `GET /orders/:id/status-history` - Get order item status history
- `GET /customers/me/orders/:id/shipments` - Get customer's order shipments

**Order Cancellation**
- `POST /customers/me/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/cancellation-requests` - Request cancellation
- `PATCH /sellers/me/order-items/:itemId/cancellation-requests/:requestId` - Approve/reject cancellation

**Order Refund**
- `POST /customers/me/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/refund-requests` - Request refund
- `PATCH /sellers/me/order-items/:itemId/refund-requests/:requestId` - Approve/reject refund

**Admin Order Oversight**
- `GET /admin/orders` - List all platform orders (paginated, filtered)
- `PATCH /admin/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/cancel` - Force cancel item
- `PATCH /admin/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/refund` - Force refund item
- `PATCH /admin/orders/:orderId/cancel` - Force cancel entire order
- `PATCH /admin/orders/:orderId/refund` - Force refund entire order

### 12. Shipping & Tracking
**Shipment Management**
- `GET /sellers/me/shipments/pending` - List pending shipments for seller
- `POST /sellers/me/shipments` - Create shipment with tracking
- `GET /sellers/me/shipments/:id` - Get specific shipment
- `PATCH /sellers/me/shipments/:id` - Update shipment

**Delivery Confirmation**
- `PATCH /customers/me/shipments/:shipmentId/confirm-delivery` - Confirm delivery
- `GET /customers/me/orders/:orderId/shipments` - Get order shipments

### 13. Reviews & Ratings
**Review Management**
- `GET /products/:id/reviews` - Get product reviews (paginated, newest first)
- `GET /products/:id/rating` - Get product average rating
- `POST /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews` - Write review
- `GET /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews` - Get customer's review for product
- `PATCH /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews/:reviewId` - Update review
- `DELETE /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews/:reviewId` - Delete review

**Review Snapshots**
- `GET /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews/:reviewId/snapshots` - Review history

### 14. Snapshot System (General)
- `GET /snapshots/:entityType/:entityId` - Get snapshots for entity
- `GET /snapshots/:entityType/:entityId/:snapshotId` - Get specific snapshot
- Access controlled based on user role (owner, admin)

## API Response Formats

**Standard Success Response**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {},
  "meta": {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-07T00:03:49.316Z",
    "requestId": "uuid"
  }
}
```

**Standard Error Response**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable message",
    "details": {}
  },
  "meta": {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-07T00:03:49.316Z",
    "requestId": "uuid"
  }
}
```

**Pagination Response**
```json
{
  "data": [],
  "meta": {
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 20,
    "total": 150,
    "totalPages": 8
  }
}
```

## Authentication & Authorization

**JWT Token Structure**
```typescript
{
  userId: string,
  role: 'customer' | 'seller' | 'admin' | 'superAdmin',
  permissions: string[],
  expiresAt: number
}
```

**Role-Based Access Control**
- Public endpoints: No authentication required
- Customer-only endpoints: `customer` role required
- Seller-only endpoints: `seller` role required
- Admin-only endpoints: `admin` or `superAdmin` role required
- Super admin-only endpoints: `superAdmin` role required

## OpenAPI 3.0 Specifications

Generate complete OpenAPI schemas including:
- All endpoint definitions with paths, methods, parameters
- Request/response schemas for each endpoint
- Authentication schemes
- Error response examples
- Request body examples

## TypeScript DTOs

Generate comprehensive TypeScript interfaces for:
- All request parameters and body DTOs
- All response DTOs
- Common types (Pagination, Error, Timestamps)
- Enum types for statuses
- Filter and sort parameter types

## API Design Constraints

1. **Resource Naming**: Use plural nouns for collections (products, orders, users)
2. **HTTP Methods**: Use standard CRUD methods (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE)
3. **Versioning**: API version in path (`/v1/...`)
4. **Status Codes**: Use appropriate HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429)
5. **Validation**: Implement comprehensive validation with clear error messages
6. **Security**: Implement rate limiting, XSS/CSRF protection, input sanitization
7. **Documentation**: Generate auto-documentation with Swagger/OpenAPI

operations.description:
Register a new customer account for the e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Purpose

This API operation enables new customers to create accounts by providing email address, password, display name, and optionally phone number. The registration process validates email format and uniqueness, stores password securely using bcrypt hashing, and creates initial customer records with pending email verification status.

## Security Implementation

The implementation follows security best practices:

- Password strength validation (minimum 8 characters, mix of letters/numbers/special characters)
- Email format validation using standard email regex patterns
- Unique email constraint enforcement to prevent duplicate registrations
- Secure password hashing using bcrypt algorithm with appropriate cost factor
- Rate limiting on registration endpoint to prevent abuse and automated attacks
- Automatic email verification token generation and email delivery upon successful registration

## Database Integration

The operation creates records in the following tables:

- **shopping_mall_customers**: Creates new customer record with hashed password, displays name, and sets is_email_verified to false initially
- **shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications**: Creates email verification record with generated token and 24-hour expiration

The database schema ensures referential integrity with CASCADE delete for email verifications when customers are deleted.

## Business Logic

- Email must be unique across all customer accounts
- Password must meet strength requirements before hashing
- Display name is required but can be updated later
- Phone number is optional but validated if provided
- Account status is set to "active" initially, allowing login after email verification
- Email verification is required before accessing certain features
- Registration IP address and user agent are logged for security auditing

## Related Operations

- After successful registration, customers should use `/auth/login` to authenticate
- If email verification expires, customers can request new verification email
- Customers can update profile information after initial registration

## Expected Behavior

On successful registration:
- Customer receives 201 Created status
- Email verification email is sent to provided address
- Account requires email verification before full functionality

On failed registration:
- Returns 400 Bad Request for validation errors
- Returns 409 Conflict if email already exists
- Provides descriptive error messages for each validation failure

Authenticate existing customer credentials and establish authenticated session.

## Purpose

This API operation validates customer login credentials against the stored password hash, generates JWT tokens for authenticated access, and creates a session record for security auditing. The system supports comprehensive session management with IP tracking and referrer information.

## Security Implementation

The implementation follows security best practices:

- Secure password verification using bcrypt compare function with constant-time comparison
- Account status validation to prevent login for banned or deleted accounts
- Rate limiting on login endpoint to prevent brute force attacks
- JWT token generation with appropriate expiration times (30 minutes for access, 7 days for refresh)
- HTTP-only cookie storage for token security
- Session tracking for security auditing and incident response

## Database Integration

The operation interacts with the following tables:

- **shopping_mall_customers**: Validates email and password hash, checks account status
- **shopping_mall_customer_sessions**: Creates new session record with connection metadata

The database schema ensures proper indexing on email for fast lookups and status for account validation.

## Business Logic

- Email must match an existing customer account
- Account status must be 'active' (not 'banned' or 'deleted')
- Password must match the stored hash after bcrypt comparison
- Login must occur within business hours if such restrictions are configured
- Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed for different devices/browsers

## Related Operations

- After successful login, customers can access protected endpoints
- If tokens expire, customers can use `/auth/refresh` to obtain new tokens
- Customers can view their active sessions and logout from all devices

## Expected Behavior

On successful login:
- Customer receives 200 OK status
- Access token and refresh token are returned
- HTTP-only cookies are set for token storage
- Session record is created in shopping_mall_customer_sessions

On failed login:
- Returns 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials
- Returns 403 Forbidden for banned or deleted accounts
- Rate limiting may return 429 Too Many Requests
- No information about whether email exists (security best practice)

operations.description:
Refresh expired authentication tokens for active customer sessions.

## Purpose

This API operation allows customers to obtain new access tokens when their current tokens expire, maintaining authenticated sessions without requiring re-authentication. The system supports token rotation and session validation for security.

## Security Implementation

The implementation follows security best practices:

- Refresh token validation with expiration check
- Session validation against shopping_mall_customer_sessions table
- Token rotation support for enhanced security
- Session invalidation tracking for logout functionality
- Rate limiting on refresh endpoint to prevent abuse

## Database Integration

The operation interacts with the following tables:

- **shopping_mall_customer_sessions**: Validates active session and token status

The database schema provides proper indexing on session expiration and customer relationships for efficient token refresh operations.

## Business Logic

- Refresh token must be valid and not expired
- Associated session must be active (not invalidated)
- Session creation timestamp must be within acceptable window
- Token refresh can occur multiple times during session lifetime
- Customers can invalidate all sessions through logout endpoint

## Related Operations

- After successful login, customers receive both access and refresh tokens
- If refresh fails, customers must use `/auth/login` to re-authenticate
- Customers can view their active sessions and logout from all devices

## Expected Behavior

On successful token refresh:
- Customer receives 200 OK status
- New access token is returned
- Session record is updated with new token metadata

On failed refresh:
- Returns 401 Unauthorized for invalid or expired refresh token
- Returns 403 Forbidden for invalidated sessions
- Customers must re-authenticate using `/auth/login`
- Logout from all devices invalidates all sessions

## Purpose

This API operation enables new customers to create accounts by providing email address, password, display name, and optionally phone number. The registration process validates email format and uniqueness, stores password securely using bcrypt hashing, and creates initial customer records with pending email verification status.

## Security Implementation

The implementation follows security best practices:

- Password strength validation (minimum 8 characters, mix of letters/numbers/special characters)
- Email format validation using standard email regex patterns
- Unique email constraint enforcement to prevent duplicate registrations
- Secure password hashing using bcrypt algorithm with appropriate cost factor
- Rate limiting on registration endpoint to prevent abuse and automated attacks
- Automatic email verification token generation and email delivery upon successful registration

## Database Integration

The operation creates records in the following tables:

- **shopping_mall_customers**: Creates new customer record with hashed password, displays name, and sets is_email_verified to false initially
- **shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications**: Creates email verification record with generated token and 24-hour expiration

The database schema ensures referential integrity with CASCADE delete for email verifications when customers are deleted.

## Business Logic

- Email must be unique across all customer accounts
- Password must meet strength requirements before hashing
- Display name is required but can be updated later
- Phone number is optional but validated if provided
- Account status is set to "active" initially, allowing login after email verification
- Email verification is required before accessing certain features
- Registration IP address and user agent are logged for security auditing

## Related Operations

- After successful registration, customers should use `/auth/login` to authenticate
- If email verification expires, customers can request new verification email
- Customers can update profile information after initial registration

## Expected Behavior

On successful registration:
- Customer receives 201 Created status
- Email verification email is sent to provided address
- Account requires email verification before full functionality

On failed registration:
- Returns 400 Bad Request for validation errors
- Returns 409 Conflict if email already exists
- Provides descriptive error messages for each validation failure

operations.description:
Renew authentication tokens for a valid super admin session on the e-commerce shopping mall platform.

This refresh endpoint allows super admins to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating, maintaining seamless access to administrative features. Super admins have ultimate system control including managing other administrators, promoting/demoting grades, and overriding platform policies.

The token refresh process validates the refresh token against the database, verifies the associated session is still active, checks account status remains 'active', and generates new JWT access tokens with extended lifetime. The system implements token rotation for security by invalidating the used refresh token and creating a new one. Session management records in shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table track the lifecycle of authentication sessions with defined expiration times.

Security considerations include token rotation to prevent token theft, validation of session validity before issuing new tokens, proper token expiration checking, and revocation of tokens for compromised accounts. The system supports session invalidation for security events like password changes or administrative actions. Token refresh is typically used when access tokens expire but the refresh token is still valid.

The system maintains comprehensive audit trails through session records with timestamps and connection metadata, enabling security monitoring and incident investigation. Refresh tokens have longer lifetimes (typically 7 days) than access tokens (typically 30 minutes) to balance security with user experience.

Related operations:
- Login operation at POST /auth/super-admin/login for initial authentication
- Logout operation for explicit session termination (if implemented)
- Session management endpoints for viewing and terminating active sessions
- Password change operation for invalidating all sessions when credentials change

1. Extract and validate refresh token from authorization header or request body
2. Look up session record in shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions using token
3. Verify session expired_at is in the future (session still valid)
4. Check associated super admin account status is 'active'
5. Verify account email_verified is true
6. Generate new JWT access token with 30-minute expiration
7. Generate new refresh token and update session record
8. Invalidate the old refresh token to prevent reuse (token rotation)
9. Return new access_token and refresh_token in response
10. Handle expired session gracefully with appropriate error response
11. Log refresh events for security auditing
12. Support bulk session invalidation for security events

This operation generates a secure password reset token that will be sent to the customer's registered email address. The token has a limited lifetime and can only be used once to change the account password.

**Security Features**:
- Tokens are generated as UUIDs for security
- Each token has a defined expiration time (typically 24 hours)
- Once used, tokens are marked as consumed and cannot be reused
- The system prevents abuse by tracking token generation frequency
- Email existence is not revealed to prevent enumeration attacks

**Workflow**:
1. Customer submits their email address
2. System validates email format
3. System generates a secure UUID token
4. Token is stored with expiration timestamp
5. Reset instructions are sent to the customer's email

This operation is the first step in the password recovery workflow. Customers may need to call this operation multiple times if their token expires or they need a new reset link.

operations.description:
Configure system-wide settings and parameters.

This endpoint allows administrators to configure platform-wide parameters that affect the entire shopping mall system. Configuration categories include:

- Shipping configuration (base fees, free shipping thresholds, carrier integrations)
- Refund policy settings (time windows, conditions, approval workflows)
- System operation flags (maintenance mode, feature toggles)
- Business rules (maximum order values, age restrictions, compliance settings)

## Security and Authorization

Only authenticated administrators with "admin" or "superAdmin" role can access this endpoint. Regular customers and sellers do not have permission to modify system configurations.

## Configuration Categories

**Shipping Configuration**
- Base shipping fee amounts
- Free shipping threshold amounts
- International shipping fees
- Carrier integration settings

**Refund Configuration**
- Refund window duration (default 7 days)
- Refund conditions and requirements
- Approval workflow settings
- Automatic refund triggers

**System Configuration**
- Maintenance mode toggle
- Feature flag management
- Performance thresholds
- Security settings

## Validation and Error Handling

- Configuration keys must follow dot notation (e.g., 'shipping.base_fee')
- Configuration values are stored as JSON strings for flexibility
- System validates configuration format and business logic constraints
- Invalid configurations are rejected with descriptive error messages

## Audit and History

All configuration changes are logged in system logs with:
- Timestamp of the change
- Admin user who made the change
- Previous and new configuration values
- Change reason (optional but recommended)

operations.description:
Delete a specific system version record from the version tracking table.

This administrative endpoint removes system version records from the shopping_mall_systematic_versions table, which tracks database migrations and component version information. This operation is typically used by system administrators for maintenance tasks such as cleaning up old version records or preparing for version rollbacks.

## Access Control
- Only super administrators have permission to execute this operation
- Regular administrators, sellers, and customers cannot access this endpoint
- The operation permanently removes the version record from the system

## Version Record Structure
The version records contain:
- Component name and version number
- Migration timestamp and description
- Active status flag
- Audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at)

## Important Considerations
- This is a permanent deletion operation
- Version history cannot be recovered after deletion
- Related snapshots and historical records may still exist
- System may have dependencies on current active versions

## Related Operations
- GET /versions: List all version records (for identifying versions to delete)
- GET /versions/:id: Get specific version details (to verify before deletion)

operations.description:
Update an existing system feature flag configuration.

This operation updates the configuration of an existing feature flag that controls A/B testing and gradual feature rollouts across the platform. Feature flags enable administrators to enable/disable features, target specific actor types, and implement gradual rollout strategies for safe feature deployment.

## Feature Flag Management

Feature flags provide comprehensive control over platform features:
- **Global Enable/Disable**: Toggle feature availability for all users
- **Targeted Access**: Restrict features to specific actor types (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin)
- **Gradual Rollout**: Implement percentage-based rollouts (0-100%) for safe deployment
- **Time-Limited Features**: Schedule features with automatic expiration

## Update Scope and Limitations

This operation updates the following feature flag properties:
- **Feature Name**: Unique identifier for the feature flag
- **Description**: Detailed explanation of the feature's purpose
- **Status**: Enable or disable the feature
- **Targeting**: Which actor types should see the feature
- **Rollout**: Percentage of eligible users who should access the feature
- **Expiration**: Optional date when the feature should auto-disable

## Authorization Requirements

Only users with appropriate administrative privileges can update feature flags. The operation validates that:
- The requesting user has super administrator or administrator privileges
- The feature flag exists and is accessible
- Update permissions are properly granted

## Validation Rules

The system enforces these validation rules:
- Feature name must follow naming convention (snake_case, unique)
- Target actor must be one of: 'all', 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', 'superAdmin'
- Rollout percentage must be between 0 and 100
- Expiration date must be in the future if provided
- Update must not violate existing feature flag constraints

operations.description:
Update an existing system feature flag configuration.

This operation updates the configuration of an existing feature flag that controls A/B testing and gradual feature rollouts across the platform. Feature flags enable administrators to enable/disable features, target specific actor types, and implement gradual rollout strategies for safe feature deployment.

## Feature Flag Management

Feature flags provide comprehensive control over platform features:
- **Global Enable/Disable**: Toggle feature availability for all users
- **Targeted Access**: Restrict features to specific actor types (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin)
- **Gradual Rollout**: Implement percentage-based rollouts (0-100%) for safe deployment
- **Time-Limited Features**: Schedule features with automatic expiration

## Update Scope and Limitations

This operation updates the following feature flag properties:
- **Feature Name**: Unique identifier for the feature flag
- **Description**: Detailed explanation of the feature's purpose
- **Status**: Enable or disable the feature
- **Targeting**: Which actor types should see the feature
- **Rollout**: Percentage of eligible users who should access the feature
- **Expiration**: Optional date when the feature should auto-disable

## Authorization Requirements

Only users with super administrator privileges can update feature flags. This operation corresponds to the shopping_mall_systematic_feature_flags table in the database, which manages system-level feature toggles for A/B testing and gradual feature rollouts. The table includes fields for feature name, description, enabled status, target actor type, rollout percentage, and optional expiration date.

## Validation Rules

The system enforces these validation rules:
- Feature name must follow naming convention (snake_case, unique)
- Target actor must be one of: 'all', 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', 'superAdmin'
- Rollout percentage must be between 0 and 100
- Expiration date must be in the future if provided
- Update must not violate existing feature flag constraints

operations.description:
Reorder product images for a specific product

This API endpoint allows authorized users to change the display order of product images. The order is critical for product presentation as it determines which image appears first in galleries and which image is used as the primary thumbnail.

## Authorization

- Sellers can reorder images for their own products
- Administrators can reorder images for any product
- Customer access is not permitted for this operation

## Implementation Details

- Validates that all image IDs belong to the specified product
- Ensures no duplicate image IDs in the reorder request
- Updates display_order field for each image based on array position
- The first image in the array gets display_order = 0
- All images must be associated with the specified product

## Business Rules

- At least one image must remain after reordering (cannot clear all images)
- All image IDs in the request must exist and belong to the specified product
- No duplicate image IDs allowed in the reorder array
- The operation maintains referential integrity with the product
operations.name: reorderImages
operations.specification:
Update display order for product images in the shopping_mall_product_images table.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Authentication & Authorization**
   - Verify user is authenticated via JWT token
   - Check if user is seller of the product OR administrator
   - Return 403 if unauthorized

2. **Input Validation**
   - Validate productId is a valid UUID format
   - Validate imageIds array is not empty
   - Validate no duplicate image IDs in the array
   - Validate all image IDs exist in database

3. **Authorization Check**
   - Query product to verify ownership (if seller)
   - Verify all images belong to the specified product
   - Return 404 if product not found
   - Return 403 if unauthorized access attempt

4. **Image Order Update**
   - Iterate through imageIds array with index
   - Update display_order for each image ID
   - First image gets display_order = 0
   - Second image gets display_order = 1, etc.
   - Use database transaction for atomic update

5. **Query Updated Images**
   - Retrieve all images for the product
   - Sort by display_order ascending
   - Return formatted image list

## Database Queries

- SELECT product WHERE id = productId (ownership verification)
- SELECT images WHERE id IN (imageIds) AND shopping_mall_product_id = productId
- UPDATE shopping_mall_product_images SET display_order = index WHERE id = imageId
- SELECT * FROM shopping_mall_product_images WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = productId ORDER BY display_order

## Error Handling

- Product not found (404)
- Unauthorized access (403)
- Invalid product ID format (400)
- Empty image array (400)
- Duplicate image IDs (400)
- Image IDs not belonging to product (400)
- Transaction failure (500)

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for an order item.

This API endpoint allows customers to request cancellation of their purchased order items. The cancellation request must include a reason explaining why the customer wants to cancel the purchase.

**Eligibility Requirements:**
- Only order items with status "paid" can be cancelled
- Items already shipped cannot be cancelled (must use refund process instead)
- Items already delivered cannot be cancelled (must use refund process instead)
- Cancellation is performed per order item, not per entire order

**Request Process:**
1. Customer initiates cancellation request with specific item and reason
2. System creates cancellation request record with timestamp and status "pending"
3. Seller receives notification of the pending cancellation request
4. Seller can approve or reject the request with explanation
5. If approved, stock quantities are restored and payment is refunded
6. If rejected, the order item continues processing normally

**Workflow Details:**
- Cancellation requests are tracked with full audit trail
- All request and response history is preserved as snapshots
- Stock restoration occurs only after approval
- Refund processing follows the same workflow as direct refunds
- Order status is recalculated after cancellation is processed

**Security Considerations:**
- Only the customer who placed the order can request cancellation
- Sellers can only respond to cancellation requests for their own products
- Administrators can force-cancel items for policy violations
- All cancellation activities are logged for dispute resolution

**Related Operations:**
- POST /sellers/me/order-items/:itemId/cancellation-requests/:requestId - Seller approves/rejects cancellation
- PATCH /admin/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/cancel - Admin force-cancel item
- POST /customers/me/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/refund-requests - Refund request (for delivered items)

operations.description:
Create a new shipment for an order item.

This operation allows sellers to register a physical shipment for one of their order items. When creating a shipment, sellers provide carrier name and tracking number information, which enables customers to track their deliveries.

## Key Features

- **One-to-One Relationship**: Each order item can have exactly one shipment (enforced by @@unique constraint)
- **Seller Association**: Shipments are linked to specific sellers for accountability
- **Tracking Integration**: Supports shipping carrier tracking numbers for delivery monitoring
- **Delivery Confirmation**: Tracks both customer-confirmed and automatic (14-day) delivery confirmations

## Security and Permissions

- Only authenticated sellers can create shipments for their own order items
- Order items must belong to the authenticated seller
- Shipment cannot be created if order item is already shipped

## Business Rules

- Cannot create shipment if order item status is not 'paid'
- Cannot create shipment if the same order item already has a shipment (one-to-one)
- Creating a shipment automatically updates order item status to 'shipped'
- Delivery confirmation happens via customer action or automatically after 14 days

## Related Operations

- GET /shipments/{id}: Retrieve specific shipment details
- PATCH /shipments/{id}: Update shipment information
- GET /orders/{id}/shipments: View all shipments for an order

Upon successful creation, update the order item status to 'shipped' and record the shipped_at timestamp.

operations.description:
Confirm receipt of a shipment.

This operation allows customers to manually confirm that they have received their shipment, marking it as delivered in the system. Delivery confirmation can also occur automatically after 14 days without customer action.

When a shipment is confirmed as delivered, the system updates the shipment status to 'delivered', sets the delivered_at timestamp, and records whether the confirmation was made by customer action or automatically. This triggers the order item status change to 'delivered' and enables review functionality for the purchased products.

Security considerations: Customers can only confirm delivery for shipments containing items from their own orders. The system validates that the shipment belongs to the requesting customer before processing confirmation.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with order and order item status tracking, ensuring proper fulfillment workflow from shipping through delivery confirmation.

- Set delivered_at to current timestamp

operations.description:
Create a refund request for a specific order item

This API endpoint allows customers to initiate a refund request for a previously delivered or shipped order item. Customers can specify their refund reason and the amount they are requesting to be refunded.

The refund request enters a pending approval workflow where the seller must review and either approve or reject the request. The system tracks the complete refund history through snapshots to maintain an immutable audit trail.

Security Considerations:
- Only the customer who purchased the order item can create a refund request
- The order item must have status "shipped" or "delivered" to be eligible for refund
- Refund requests must be submitted within the allowed time window (typically 7 days for delivered items)
- Sellers are notified when new refund requests are created for their products

   - shopping_mall_order_item_id from path parameter

   - customer_reason from request body
   - requested_refund_amount from request body
   - status: "pending"
   - timestamps (created_at, updated_at)
5. Return the created refund request with full details

operations.description:
Delete a customer review for a product.

This operation permanently removes a customer review from the platform. Reviews can be deleted by the customer who wrote the review or by administrators for policy violations.

**Security and Authorization**

- Only the customer who wrote the review can delete their own review
- Administrators can delete any review for policy violations
- Review snapshots are created before deletion to preserve audit history
- The original review content and rating are preserved in snapshots for historical accuracy

**Snapshot Preservation**

When a review is deleted:
- A complete snapshot of the review state is created at the time of deletion
- The snapshot preserves the rating, text content, and timestamp
- The snapshot links to the original review for audit trail purposes
- Review snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted

**Related Operations**

- `GET /products/:id/reviews` retrieves product reviews including deleted ones (marked as deleted)
- `GET /products/:id/rating` recalculates average rating excluding deleted reviews
- `POST /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews` create new reviews for products
- `PATCH /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews/:reviewId` edit existing reviews

**Error Handling**

The operation may return the following error codes:
- `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`: Review does not exist
- `REVIEW_NOT_AUTHOR`: Customer attempted to delete another customer's review
- `REVIEW_DELETE_FAILED`: Review deletion failed due to system error
- `REVIEW_HAS_PENDING_REFUND`: Review associated with pending refund request
- `REVIEW_HAS_PENDING_CANCELLATION`: Review associated with pending cancellation request
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a customer review and create a snapshot for audit purposes.

Query the shopping_mall_reviews table by the provided reviewId.
Verify that the current user is either the review author or an administrator.
If verification passes, create a snapshot in the shopping_mall_review_snapshots table with:
- Current review rating
- Current review content (or '[review deleted]' if already deleted)
- Current timestamp as edited_at if editing, or null if immediate deletion
- Current timestamp as created_at for the snapshot
- Link to the original review ID
- Link to the customer who wrote the review
- Link to the product that was reviewed

After snapshot creation, permanently delete the review record from shopping_mall_reviews.
Update the product's average rating by recalculating from remaining reviews.
Return the deleted review as a summary with fields: id, customer_id, order_item_id, rating, content, deleted status, and timestamps.

responseBody.description: Summary of the deleted review with essential information

operations.description:
Manage product reviews for seller's products

This operation provides comprehensive review management capabilities for sellers to oversee and maintain reviews for their products. Sellers can view, update, and manage customer reviews associated with their products in the shopping mall platform.

## Access Control

This operation is available only to authenticated sellers. Sellers can only manage reviews for products they own or have explicit permission to manage. Customer reviews are protected data that must be handled with appropriate authorization.

## Review Management Operations

The endpoint supports multiple review management operations through the request body:

- **List Reviews**: Retrieve all reviews for seller's products with filtering and pagination
- **Update Review Content**: Modify review text content and rating (if allowed by business rules)
- **Delete Review**: Remove inappropriate or invalid reviews (admin override capability)
- **Flag Review**: Mark reviews for administrative review

## Data Integrity Considerations

Review management must maintain data integrity and audit trails. All review modifications create snapshots preserving the previous state. Reviews can only be modified by the original author or sellers with appropriate administrative permissions.

## Business Rules

- Reviews can only be managed for products owned by the authenticated seller
- Review deletion requires appropriate authorization level
- System may enforce review modification windows based on delivery date
- Some reviews may be protected from modification based on platform policies

## Related Operations

- Customers use `GET /products/:id/reviews` to view product reviews
- Customers use `POST /customers/me/products/:productId/reviews` to write new reviews
- System administrators use `PATCH /admin/reviews/:id` for oversight and enforcement actions

operations.specification:
Implement comprehensive review management endpoint for sellers.

## Service Logic

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify seller authentication and extract seller ID
2. **Authorization Validation**: Ensure seller has permission to manage reviews for specified products
3. **Request Processing** based on action type:
   - **LIST**: Query shopping_mall_reviews table with seller product filter, pagination, and sorting
   - **UPDATE**: Modify review content if authorized and within modification window
   - **DELETE**: Remove review if seller owns product or has admin permissions
4. **Audit Trail**: Create review snapshots for all modifications
5. **Response Formatting**: Return paginated results with review details and seller permissions

## Database Operations

- Query shopping_mall_reviews table joined with shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_products
- Filter by seller's products using seller_id in product table
- Support filtering by product_id, rating, date range, and review status
- Implement pagination with offset/limit or cursor-based approach
- Update review content and rating fields for authorized sellers
- Soft delete reviews or mark as deleted based on business requirements

## Validation Rules

- Verify seller owns or manages the product associated with review
- Check modification windows (e.g., reviews can only be modified within 7 days of delivery)
- Validate rating range (1-5 stars) for updates
- Ensure proper authorization levels for deletion operations
- Prevent sellers from modifying their own reviews (conflict of interest)

## Edge Cases

- Handle reviews for deleted products gracefully
- Support bulk operations for multiple reviews
- Implement rate limiting for review management actions
- Handle concurrent modifications through versioning
- Return appropriate error codes for unauthorized access attempts

operations.description:
Retrieve the average rating and review count for a specific product.

This endpoint provides product rating metrics that help customers evaluate product quality before making purchase decisions. The average rating is calculated from customer reviews and displayed as a decimal value (e.g., 4.5 stars) on a 1.0-5.0 scale.

## Rating System Overview

The shopping mall platform implements a comprehensive product rating system where customers can rate products on a 5-star scale after completing purchases. These ratings are aggregated and stored in the product_review_ratings table to provide quick access to rating information without real-time calculations.

## Business Purpose

- **Customer Decision Support**: Helps potential buyers evaluate product quality before purchase
- **Product Visibility**: Higher-rated products may receive preferential placement in search results
- **Seller Feedback**: Provides sellers with aggregate feedback on their products
- **Quality Assurance**: Enables identification of products that may need quality improvements

## Rating Calculation Methodology

- Average ratings are calculated from all non-deleted customer reviews for each product
- The calculation excludes reviews that have been soft-deleted by their authors
- Ratings are updated automatically when reviews are added, edited, or removed
- The system maintains a running average for efficient retrieval
- The rating table itself has a deleted_at field for soft deletion of the rating record

## Display Considerations

- Average ratings are typically displayed alongside product listings in search results
- Product detail pages show the complete rating breakdown with star visualizations
- Sellers can view their products' average ratings in their dashboard
- Administrators can review overall rating patterns across their platform

## Related Endpoints

- `GET /products/{id}/reviews` - Retrieve individual customer reviews for detailed feedback
- `GET /customers/me/products/{productId}/reviews` - Check if customer has already reviewed the product
- `GET /products` - Search and filter products with rating-based sorting options

## Performance Optimization

This endpoint queries a pre-aggregated table rather than calculating ratings in real-time, ensuring fast response times even with large numbers of reviews. The database maintains the rating metrics automatically through triggers or scheduled updates.

operations.description:

The validation process involves checking each cart item against current product data, verifying stock availability, confirming product availability status, and ensuring all items belong to active sellers. operations.specification:
Cart validation service method that performs comprehensive pre-checkout validation.

Process:
1. Retrieve customer's cart items with full product and variant data
2. For each cart item, validate: product active status, seller active status, variant availability
3. Check stock quantities match cart quantities (or provide warnings)
4. Verify all items can be shipped to customer's address
5. Validate product pricing and availability
6. Generate comprehensive validation report with issues and warnings
7. Calculate overall cart readiness status

Edge cases:
- Handle carts with no items (return ready status)
- Support partial validation (only check specific items if requested)
- Handle concurrent stock changes (show warnings for stale data)
- Support multiple shipping addresses in cart

Business rules:
- Out of stock items: Mark as error, prevent checkout
- Low stock items: Show warning with current quantity
- Deleted products: Mark as error, suggest removal
- Inactive sellers: Mark as error, contact support
- Price changes: Show warning with original vs current price
- Product unavailable: Mark as error with reason

operations.description:
Add product variant to customer shopping cart

This operation allows authenticated customers to add specific product variants to their shopping cart for potential future purchase. The shopping cart serves as an intermediate state between product browsing and final order placement, enabling customers to collect multiple items before proceeding to checkout.

The operation handles several important business rules:

- **Duplicate Prevention**: If the same variant is already in the cart, quantities are combined rather than creating duplicate entries, ensuring clean cart management
- **Stock Validation**: The system validates that sufficient stock is available before adding the item, preventing invalid cart additions
- **Customer Ownership**: Cart items are automatically associated with the authenticated customer, ensuring proper cart isolation between users
- **Availability Monitoring**: Cart items remain synchronized with product availability - items become unavailable if variants are deleted or run out of stock
- **Quantity Management**: Customers can later modify quantities or remove items from their cart before checkout

From a user experience perspective, this operation enables the core shopping workflow where customers can browse products, add items to their cart for review, adjust quantities, and eventually proceed to checkout when ready to purchase. The cart serves as a temporary holding area that preserves customers' selection while they continue shopping or prepare for final purchase.

The cart item lifecycle includes creation with quantity selection, potential quantity modifications, availability updates as stock changes, and eventual removal either through successful order placement (which clears the cart) or manual deletion by the customer.

If cart item already exists for same variant, increment quantity instead of creating duplicate. Link cart item to authenticated customer's profile automatically. operations.description:
Validate product availability and stock levels for shopping cart items.

This operation provides comprehensive availability checking for product variants in the shopping cart system. It validates current stock quantities against requested purchase quantities and returns detailed availability status including warnings, constraints, and stock information.

## Purpose and Overview

The availability checking endpoint serves as a critical validation layer in the shopping cart workflow. Before customers proceed to checkout, they can validate that their selected variants are available in the desired quantities. This prevents failed checkouts due to stock issues and provides customers with real-time inventory information.

## Availability Status Types

The operation returns several availability states for each variant:

- **available**: Requested quantity is fully available
- **low_stock**: Some stock available but below threshold (typically < 10 units)
- **limited_stock**: Requested quantity partially available but less than requested
- **unavailable**: No stock available for the variant

## Stock Constraint Handling

The system enforces several stock constraints:

- Maximum quantity per variant is limited by available stock
- Out-of-stock variants are marked as unavailable
- Low stock warnings are shown when quantity falls below threshold
- Deleted variants are marked as unavailable

## Integration with Cart Operations

This availability check is typically called:

1. When adding items to cart (real-time validation)
2. Before checkout (comprehensive cart validation)
3. Periodically during cart session (stock freshness checks)

Related operations that should be used with this endpoint:

- `GET /customers/me/cart` - View current cart items for validation
- `POST /customers/me/cart` - Add variants to cart after availability check
- `PATCH /customers/me/cart/items/:itemId` - Update quantities after availability verification

## Business Logic and Validation

The availability check follows these business rules:

1. Stock levels are calculated from inventory history records
2. Stock updates in real-time based on recent transactions
3. Deleted variants return unavailable status immediately
4. Out-of-stock variants show availability warning

## Security Considerations

Availability checking is a public operation - any authenticated user can validate stock levels. However, actual stock data is protected and only available through this controlled validation endpoint.
operations.name: validateCartAvailability
operations.specification:
Validate product availability and stock levels for shopping cart items by querying the shopping_mall_inventory_histories and shopping_mall_product_variants tables.

Implementation Steps:
1. Accept request with variant IDs and requested quantities
2. Query shopping_mall_product_variants for each variant to get current stock_quantity
3. Query shopping_mall_inventory_histories for active stock calculations if needed
4. Compare requested quantity with available stock_quantity
5. Calculate availability status: available, low_stock, limited_stock, or unavailable
6. Apply business logic thresholds (low_stock_threshold = 10)
7. Return comprehensive availability information for each variant
8. Include warnings for stock constraints and business rules

Database Queries:
- SELECT stock_quantity FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE id IN (:variantIds) AND is_active = true
- SELECT SUM(quantity) as stock FROM shopping_mall_inventory_histories WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id IN (:variantIds) AND deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY shopping_mall_product_variant_id

Business Rules:
- Stock quantity = sum of all non-deleted inventory history records
- Low stock threshold = 10 units
- Out of stock = stock_quantity <= 0
- Limited stock = requested > available && available > 0

Edge Cases:
- Handle variants that have been deleted (return unavailable)
- Handle variants that are inactive (return unavailable)
- Handle inventory calculation edge cases (empty history = 0 stock)

requestBody.description: Availability validation requests containing variant IDs and requested quantities

responseBody.description: Availability validation results for each requested variant

The shipment record contains information about the entire delivery process:
- Initial creation with shipping address
- Tracking information addition (carrier and tracking number)

- Complete audit trail of shipment status changes

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific shipment.

This API endpoint provides comprehensive shipment information including tracking details, carrier information, delivery status, and the shipping address. It is designed for both customers to track their orders and sellers to manage their shipments.

## Access Control
- Customer users can access shipments containing their own order items
- Seller users can access shipments they are responsible for shipping
- Admin and Super Admin users can access all shipments for platform oversight

## Shipment Lifecycle
The shipment record contains information about the entire delivery process:
- Initial creation with shipping address
- Tracking information addition (carrier and tracking number)
- Delivery confirmation (customer action or automatic after 14 days)
- Complete audit trail of shipment status changes

## Related Operations
- `PATCH /shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery` - Confirm delivery of this shipment
- `GET /orders/{orderId}/shipments` - Get all shipments for an order
- `GET /sellers/me/shipments` - Get shipments for current seller

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive tracking history for shipments with all status changes and delivery events.

This operation provides detailed tracking history showing the complete journey of shipments from initial processing through final delivery. It tracks all status changes, transit events, and delivery confirmations in chronological order, enabling comprehensive shipment monitoring and delivery verification.

The tracking history includes timestamped events showing when shipments were created, processed, shipped, in transit, out for delivery, and delivered. Each tracking event includes location information, status changes, and any relevant notes or updates from shipping carriers.

operations.description:
Update a shipping shipment record with tracking information.

This operation allows sellers to update shipment tracking information for orders they are responsible for shipping. It supports updating carrier name, tracking number, and shipment status through a comprehensive tracking workflow that integrates with order management and delivery confirmation systems.

The shipment tracking system enables real-time delivery monitoring, automatic delivery confirmation after 14 days if customer doesn't manually confirm, and provides complete audit trail of all shipment status changes. This ensures transparency between sellers, customers, and platform administrators throughout the delivery process.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive review analytics for a specific product.

This endpoint provides detailed analytics and statistical information about customer reviews for a specific product. It aggregates review data to deliver insights including average ratings, review volume, rating distribution across all star levels, and temporal analysis of review patterns.

## Key Features

- **Aggregated Statistics**: Calculate and return the average rating score across all non-deleted reviews for the specified product
- **Review Volume Metrics**: Show total review count and breakdown by time period (daily, weekly, monthly trends)
- **Rating Distribution**: Display the distribution of ratings across all star levels (1-star through 5-star counts)
- **Temporal Analysis**: Provide review activity patterns over time for trend identification
- **Seller Context**: Include seller-specific review statistics when accessed by the product's seller

## Security and Authorization

- **Public Access**: Basic analytics (average rating, review count) available to all users
- **Seller Access**: Sellers viewing their own product analytics receive additional insights
- **Admin Access**: Administrators receive complete analytics including sensitive data
- **Authorization**: Check user role and permissions before returning analytics data

## Database Relationships

This endpoint queries the following database tables:
- {@link shopping_mall_products.id}: The product being analyzed
- {@link shopping_mall_reviews}: Individual customer reviews with ratings and content
- {@link shopping_mall_product_review_ratings}: Pre-calculated aggregated rating metrics

## Business Logic

- Only non-deleted reviews are included in calculations
- Deleted reviews are completely excluded from all analytics
- Average rating is calculated as arithmetic mean of all valid ratings
- Rating distribution provides histogram of review ratings
- Temporal analysis shows review activity patterns for trend identification

## Related Operations

- {@link GET /products/{productId}/reviews}: Retrieve individual reviews
- {@link GET /products/{productId}/rating}: Get simplified product rating
- {@link GET /sellers/me/products}: List seller's products for analytics view
- {@link GET /admin/products}: Admin endpoint for product oversight

## Error Handling

- Returns 404 if product not found
- Returns 403 if unauthorized access to seller-specific analytics
- Returns appropriate error codes for database or calculation errors

## Implementation Notes

This endpoint is designed for quick, cached analytics delivery. For detailed review analysis or real-time calculations, use the individual reviews endpoint.

operations.description:
Write a product review for a delivered order item

This endpoint allows customers to submit reviews for products they have purchased and received. Reviews include a star rating (1-5) and optional text content that provides feedback about the purchased product.

Security and Authorization:
- Only customers who purchased the specific order item can write a review
- The system validates that the customer has actually purchased the item
- Each order item can have only one review per customer (enforced by unique constraint)
- Reviews cannot be written for items that have not been delivered yet

Database Integration:
The operation creates a record in the shopping_mall_reviews table with the customer's ID (from authentication), the order item ID (from path parameter), the rating score, and optional content text. The system automatically generates the review ID and creation timestamp.

Business Rules:
- Rating must be an integer between 1 and 5 (inclusive)
- Content is optional but cannot exceed maximum length if implemented
- Review can only be written after the order item status is 'delivered'
- Attempting to write multiple reviews for the same order item will result in a conflict error
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table.
1. Extract customer_id from JWT authentication token
2. Validate that orderId and itemId path parameters are valid UUIDs
3. Query shopping_mall_order_items table to verify:
   - Order item exists with matching orderId and itemId
   - Order item.customer_id matches authenticated customer_id (ownership verification)
   - Order item status is 'delivered' (review eligibility)
4. Validate request body:
   - rating is required, must be integer between 1-5
   - content is optional, must be string if provided
5. Create review record with:
   - id: generated UUID
   - customer_id: from authentication
   - order_item_id: from path parameter
   - rating: from request body
   - content: from request body (nullable)
   - created_at: current timestamp
6. Update product_review_ratings table to recalculate average rating
7. Return complete review record with all database-generated fields

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
